why.text: Atlantic and Mediterranean climates meet here, giving mild temperatures and about 400 mm of rain. That suits full-bodied reds made for ageing.

styles.text: Dry and semi-dry whites, rosados and reds, plus semi-sweet and sweet whites and rosados; reds sold young or aged.

climate.text: Atlantic and Mediterranean influences meet; temperatures are mild and annual rainfall is about 400 mm.

soil.text: Clay-limestone (a quarter), ferrous clay (a quarter) and alluvial soils near the rivers (half).

tastes.text: Reds: purple when young, cherry-garnet as crianza, ruby-brick as gran reserva; intense fruit, toasted oak, then spice with age. Whites: pale straw with lemon-green rims; green fruit, flowers. Rosés: strawberry; red fruit, floral notes.

styles.name: Crianza
styles.text: Reds aged at least two years, a year of it in oak barrel.

styles.name: Reserva
styles.text: Reds aged 36 months in oak and bottle, at least 12 in barrel.

styles.name: Gran Reserva
styles.text: Reds aged 60 months in oak and bottle, at least 24 in barrel.

why.text: Rioja Alta gets Atlantic influence and more rain. Its reds are medium-strength with high acidity, suited to barrel ageing.

styles.text: Reds with body and high acidity, suited to barrel ageing; whites and rosados can also carry the zone name.

climate.text: Mainly Atlantic: more rain and fewer sunshine hours than the south, sheltered by the Sierra de Cantabria.

soil.text: A mix of clay-limestone, ferrous clay and alluvial soils.

tastes.text: Reds of medium strength with full body and high acidity, suited to barrel ageing.

why.text: Atlantic and Mediterranean climates meet behind the Sierra de Cantabria. The wines are slightly riper, with a little less acidity, to drink young or age.

styles.text: Versatile reds to drink young or age, good for blending; whites and rosados can also carry the zone name.

climate.text: Atlantic meets Mediterranean; sunshine like Rioja Alta, a little less rain; the Sierra de Cantabria shelters it from the north.

soil.text: Clay-limestone soils on terraces and in small plots.

tastes.text: Reds a little stronger and less acidic than in Rioja Alta; versatile, for early drinking or for ageing.

why.text: A drier, warmer Mediterranean climate with more sun gives riper, fuller reds. They suit blending and barrel ageing.

styles.text: Riper, fuller reds for blending and barrel ageing, some to drink young; zone wines need higher minimum alcohol.

climate.text: Clearly Mediterranean: drier and warmer, with less rain and generally more sunshine than the rest of Rioja.

soil.text: Mainly alluvial and ferrous clay soils.

tastes.text: Warmer, drier site: reds with higher strength and extract, for blending into barrel-aged wines or drinking young.
